messages:
jamie: FYI hitting a weird onboarding loop with the Go sample app. After the token refresh path runs we get a 500 with body `\"auth failure\"` and the SDK treats it as retryable -> infinite backoff loop.

maria-pe: ugh. which SDK version?

jamie: go sdk v0.9.7 from the quickstart. repro steps: run `make run-demo` -> wait for refresh token expiry -> trigger a request. Logs attached below.

jamie: logs:
```
2026-03-22T14:02:13Z INFO auth: refreshing token
2026-03-22T14:02:13Z ERROR transport: request failed status=500 body=\"auth failure\"
2026-03-22T14:02:13Z WARN sdk: retrying; attempt=1 backoff=200ms
```

cheng: Can you paste the HTTP response headers too? curious if upstream returned `Retry-After` or any `WWW-Authenticate` info.

jamie: header dump: `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Request-Id: r-03`, no `Retry-After`, no `WWW-Authenticate`.

lucas: sounds like two issues folded together: (1) the runtime should emit 401 for auth failures not 500, and (2) SDK must map 401 -> AuthError (non-retryable by default) and provide a helper to trigger token refresh. Right now Go treats any 5xx as transient.

maria-pe: agree. For onboarding the UX is bad: users see the demo hang with backoff and think the platform is flaky. We should special-case our auth-related error shape.

jamie: minimal proposal: if response body matches `/auth/i` or headers include `WWW-Authenticate` -> map to typed `AuthError` with `retryable: false` and `hint: \"refresh token and retry\"`. Also surface the server request-id in SDK error to help ops.

cheng: +1 but prefer relying on status code first. If runtime returns 500 we should still try to classify by structured error body. Can we standardize runtime error JSON like:
```json
{"code":"auth.invalid_token","message":"refresh failed: token expired","meta":{"request_id":"r-03"}}
```
so SDKs can parse `code` and decide mapping.

lucas: this collides with quickstart where people often run against proxies. SDK must also expose a fallback classifier: `IsAuthError(resp)` that checks status, code, and message regex.

maria-pe: action items: 1) eng-runtime to consider returning 401 + structured error for auth failures, 2) SDK team to add classifier and typed `AuthError` in v0.9.8, 3) docs/update quickstart to mention token refresh handling.

jamie: created an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/458 (proto) and a Go SDK PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/232 (wip).

cheng: I'll take the runtime ticket. I'll add a regression test to ensure auth failures are 401 and include `code: auth.invalid_token`.

lucas: SDK owners: pinging @maria-pe and @jamie for a spec. Also add a small sample app snippet to the quickstart that shows how to call `client.AuthRefresh()` on AuthError.

maria-pe: will draft spec and update the sample app. Also add a note for streaming: if a streaming response fails with an auth error mid-stream, SDK should emit an `AuthError` event and stop retries automatically.

jamie: thanks. one more tiny UX ask: include a `retry_hint` field in the typed error (values: `none`, `refresh_token`, `rate_limit`) so that sample apps can present clear next steps.

lucas: good idea. Put that in the spec PR.

sdk-bot: New issue created: runtime#458 by cheng. New PR opened: go-sdk#232 by jamie (draft).

maria-pe: leaving notes here so PMs can triage. tagging @product for prioritization. :hand-up:

jamie: and I'll update the onboarding bug tracker with a link to the demo repro and mark it P2.

cheng: starting the runtime patch now, ETA EOD tomorrow.

lucas: thanks team. once spec PR lands we'll cut a go-sdk v0.9.8 release and roll the quickstart docs. :shipit:
